'''Franz Jacob Wagner''' (born 27 August 2001) is a German professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]].

Wagner, a native of [[Berlin]], started his career with [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL) club [[Alba Berlin]]. In 2019, he was named [[Basketball Bundesliga Best German Young Player|BBL Best German Young Player]]. Wagner has played for the German youth national teams, winning a gold medal at the 2018 [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]].

His older brother [[Moritz Wagner (basketball)|Moritz Wagner]], a former Michigan standout, plays for the [[Brooklyn Nets]].

==Professional career==
===Alba Berlin (2017–2019)===
In the 2018–19 season, Wagner played on a dual contract for both [[Alba Berlin]] in the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL), the top German league, and SSV Lokomotive Bernau in the third-tier [[ProB]] league. In May 2019, he won the [[Basketball Bundesliga Best German Young Player|BBL Best Young Player Award]].<ref>{{cite web |title=easyCredit – Franz Wagner |url=https://www.easycredit-bbl.de/de/n/news/2019/mai/franz-wagner--bester-deutscher-nachwuchsspieler-u22-/ |work=easycredit-bbl.de |accessdate=May 13, 2019}}</ref> In Game 2 of the BBL Finals against [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]], Wagner scored a team-high 14 points, making all six of his shots.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bayern vor der Titelverteidigung? München holt sich mit 82:77 in Berlin den zweiten Sieg in der Finalserie |url=https://www.easycredit-bbl.de/de/n/spielberichte/2018-2019/nachbericht/2019-06-19-ber-fcb/ |work=easycredit-bbl.de |accessdate=June 21, 2019}}</ref> By the end of the season, he was averaging 4.6 points in 12.4 minutes per game in the BBL and played limited minutes in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref name="realgm">{{cite web |title=Franz Wagner Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Franz-Wagner/Summary/108861 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=September 2, 2019}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2021–present)===
====2021–22: All-Rookie honors====
[[File:Wagner2022.jpg|thumb|upright|Wagner with the Orlando Magic in 2022]]
Wagner was selected with the eighth pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Zuke |first1=Ryan |title=Franz Wagner becomes Michigan basketball's first top-10 pick since 2014, drafted by Orlando Magic |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2021/07/franz-wagner-becomes-michigan-basketballs-first-top-10-pick-since-2014-drafted-by-orlando-magic.html |access-date=July 30, 2021 |work=[[MLive Media Group|MLive.com]] |date=July 29, 2021}}</ref> He and fellow lottery pick [[Jalen Suggs]] signed with the Magic on August 3.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-jalen-suggs-franz-wagner-nba-draft-contract-20210803|title=Orlando Magic Sign Jalen Suggs and Franz Wagner|accessdate=May 21, 2022|date=August 3, 2021|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref> Wagner posted his first NBA double-double with a career-high 11 rebounds and 14 points as well as 6 assists on December 18 against the [[2021-22 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Magic 100, Nets 93: Magic prevail in battle of two undermanned teams |url=https://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2021/12/19/22844604/orlando-magic-brooklyn-nets-chuma-okeke-robin-lopez-franz-wagner |accessdate=May 5, 2022 |date=December 19, 2021 |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |author=Cali, Mike |archive-date=March 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220311010320/https://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2021/12/19/22844604/orlando-magic-brooklyn-nets-chuma-okeke-robin-lopez-franz-wagner |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 27, 2021, Wagner put up a career-high 38 points in a 127–110 loss to the [[2021–22 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Bell|first=Justin |date=December 27, 2021 |title=Magic rookie Franz Wagner's monster night hits milestone franchise hasn't seen in 31 years |url=https://clutchpoints.com/magic-news-magic-rookie-franz-wagners-monster-night-hits-milestone-franchise-hasnt-seen-in-31-years/|website=ClutchPoints|access-date=January 1, 2022}}</ref> Wagner was named the NBA Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in December.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-rookies-month-december-josh-giddey-franz-wagner|title=Franz Wagner, Dishes 10 assists in loss|work=[[CBS Sports]] |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-franz-wagner-dishes-10-assists-in-loss/ |date=January 12, 2022|access-date=May 5, 2022}}</ref> This marked the first time a Magic rookie forward had ever posted 10 or more assists in a game.<ref>{{cite web|title=@OrlandoMagic status update|via=[[Twitter]]|url=https://twitter.com/OrlandoMagic/status/1481453041089978371?r|date=January 12, 2022|access-date=May 5, 2022}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=December 2023}} Following the [[2021–22 NBA season]] he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Barnes, Cunningham, Mobley headline 2021–22 Kia NBA All-Rookie 1st ====2022–24: Steady improvement====
On November 5, 2022, Wagner scored a season-high 31 points and recorded six assists in a 126–123 overtime loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Magic's Franz Wagner: Season-high 31 points |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-franz-wagner-season-high-31-points/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=December 31, 2022 |date=November 5, 2022}}</ref> On December 29, he was suspended by the NBA for one game without pay due to coming off the bench during an altercation in a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]] the day before.<ref>{{cite web |title=NBA announces suspensions from Pistons-Magic game |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-pistons-magic-suspensions |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=December 31, 2022 |date=December 29, 2022}}</ref> Wagner finished his sophomore season averaging 18.6 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 3.5 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Franz Wagner Stats, News, Bio |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4566434/franz-wagner |access-date=May 1, 2023 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

In his third season, Wagner played 72 games for the Magic, posting career highs across the board with 19.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 3.7 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Franz Wagner Player Profile |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1630532/franz-wagner/bio |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 23, 2025}}</ref> On April 27, 2024, Wagner recorded 34 points on 13-of-17 shooting and 13 rebounds, securing his first playoff double-double to lead the Magic to a 112–89 victory over the Cavaliers in Game 4, tying the series 2–2.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Magic Tie Series 2-2 After Comeback vs. Cavaliers |date=April 27, 2024 |url=https://www.si.com/nba/magic/news/magic-cavaliers-2024-nba-playoffs-game-4-game-recap-final-score |access-date=April 27, 2024 |publisher=Sports Illustrated}}</ref>

====2024–present: Breakthrough====
On July 6, 2024, the Magic signed Wagner to a contract extension reportedly worth $224 million.<ref>{{cite web |title=Magic, Franz Wagner agree to five‑year maximum contract extension |url=https://www.nba.com/news/magic-franz-wagner-max-extension |website=NBA.com |date=2024-07-05 |access-date=2024-07-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Franz Wagner to Contract Extension|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-franz-wagner-to-contract-extension-20240706|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 6, 2024|date=July 6, 2024}}</ref>

On November 18, 2024, Wagner earned his first NBA Eastern Conference Player of the Week Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-franz-wagner-named-nba-eastern-conference-player-of-the-week-20241118|title=Orlando Magic's Franz Wagner Named NBA's Eastern Conference Player of the Week|accessdate=December 18, 2024|date=November 18, 2024|work=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 21, Wagner had a season-high 37 points, along with six rebounds, 11 assists, four steals and scored a game-winning three-pointer in a 119–118 victory against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Woike|first=Dan|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2024-11-21/lakers-lose-orlando-magic-lebron-wagner|title=Lakers' six-game winning streak ends in late collapse to Orlando Magic|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=November 21, 2024|access-date=November 28, 2024}}</ref> On December 6, Wagner put up 30 points, five rebounds, five assists, one steal, and one block in a 102–94 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He achieved his third-consecutive 30-point game for the second time in his career, joining [[Shaquille O'Neal]] and [[Tracy McGrady]] as the only players in Magic franchise history to score at least 30 points in at least three consecutive games multiple times.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/magic-news-franz-wagner-joins-shaquille-oneal-tracy-mcgrady|title=Franz Wagner joins Shaquille O'Neal, Tracy McGrady amid blistering scoring stretch|website=ClutchPoints|last=Ojeda|first=Julian|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=July 7, 2024}}</ref> On December 7, 2024, it was announced that Wagner had suffered from a torn right [[Abdominal oblique muscles|oblique]], an injury which teammate [[Paolo Banchero]] suffered earlier in the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-07 |title=Magic's Franz Wagner suffers same injury as Paolo Banchero |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2024/12/07/orlando-magic-franz-wagner-paolo-banchero-injury-update-jeff-weltman-nba-76ers-suns-jamahl-mosley/ |access-date=2024-12-07 |website=Orlando Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref> Wagner returned on January 23, 2025, scoring 20 points in a 101–79 loss against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 23, 2025 |title=Trail Blazers win third straight, beat Magic 100-79 to spoil Franz Wagner's return for Orlando |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705188 |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On November 22, 2025, Wagner scored a season-high 37 points, grabbed 6 rebounds, and dished 7 assists to lead the Magic to a 133–121 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Starting 5: 12 In A Row! Pistons Extend Streak, Harden Drops 55, Jokić & Russ Duel |website=NBA.com |date=November 23, 2025 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/starting-5-12-in-a-row-pistons-extend-streak-harden-drops-55-jokic-russ-duel |access-date=November 23, 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Franz Wagner (basketball).jpg|thumb|Wagner with the [[Germany national under-19 basketball team|German U18 team]] at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]] in 2018]]
Wagner played for [[Germany national under-17 basketball team|Germany]] at the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Podgorica]], Montenegro. In five games, he averaged 7.4 points per game as his team finished in 13th place.<ref>{{cite web |title=Franz Jacob Wagner (GER)'s profile – FIBA U16 European Championship Division A 2017 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/player/Franz-Jacob-Wagner |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=September 2, 2019}}</ref> In 2018, Wagner averaged six points per game and helped Germany win the gold medal at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], an under-18 competition in [[Mannheim]], Germany.<ref name="sang">{{cite web |last1=Sang |first1=Orion |title=Franz Wagner, brother of Moritz, picks Wolverines |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2019/07/06/michigan-basketball-recruiting-franz-wagner/1537637001/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |accessdate=September 2, 2019 |date=July 6, 2019}}</ref> In the [[2019 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in [[Volos]], Greece, he averaged 13 points and 4.8 rebounds per game, leading his team to 11th place. He missed one game with a back injury.<ref name="burkhardt">{{cite web |last1=Burkhardt |first1=Dylan |title=What we learned about Franz Wagner at FIBA U18 Euros |url=https://umhoops.com/2019/08/05/what-we-learned-about-franz-wagner-at-fiba-u18-euros/ |publisher=UM Hoops |accessdate=September 2, 2019 |date=August 5, 2019}}</ref> In [[EuroBasket 2022]], he averaged 16.1 points and 4 rebounds per game, beating Poland in his home city of Berlin to take home bronze for Germany.<ref name="mickens">{{cite web |last1=Mickens |first1=Jorie |title=Franz 'The Wunderkind' Wagner shines in EuroBasket tournament |url=https://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2022/9/16/23357244/franz-wagner-orlando-magic-eurobasket-tournament/ |work=Orlando Pinstriped Post |accessdate=November 21, 2022 |date=September 16, 2022 |archive-date=February 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230204195255/https://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2022/9/16/23357244/franz-wagner-orlando-magic-eurobasket-tournament |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2023, Wagner became world champion, winning gold at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] with the German national team. It was the first time that Germany won this event. In recognition of his individual play, Wagner was named to the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|All-FIBA World Cup Second Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/news/world-cup-2023-all-second-team-best-coach-and-best-defensive-player-awards-revealed|title=World Cup 2023 All-Second Team, Best Coach and Best Defensive Player Awards revealed|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=September 10, 2023|access-date=September 15, 2023}}</ref>

At the [[2024 Olympics]], after going unbeaten in Group B and winning over Greece in the quarterfinals, Germany lost to France, 69–73, in the semifinals. In the bronze medal game, Germany lost to Serbia 83–93. Wagner averaged 18.5 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.0 steals in 6 games played. For his play, he was named to the tournament's All-Second Team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-10 |title=Gilgeous-Alexander, Bogdanovic, F. Wagner, Yabusele, Antetokounmpo named to Paris 2024 All-Second Team |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/gilgeous-alexander-bogdanovic-f-wagner-yabusele-antetokounmpo-named-to-paris |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref>

At the [[EuroBasket 2025]], the [[Germany men's national basketball team]] won the gold medal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 September 2025 |title=Germany win incredible Final against Türkiye |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/germany-win-incredible-final-against-tuerkiye-eb-25 |access-date=16 September 2025 |publisher=FIBA}}</ref> Wagner and teammate [[Dennis Schröder]] were on the [[FIBA EuroBasket All-Tournament Team]] 1st team along with [[Luka Dončić]], [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] and [[Alperen Şengün]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 September 2025 |title=All-Star Five: Schroder, Doncic, Wagner, Antetokounmpo, Sengun |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/all-star-five-schroder-doncic-wagner-antetokounmpo-sengun |access-date=16 September 2025 |publisher=FIBA}}</ref>
